## Definition

"Gentrification is a process whereby the urban working class and poor are expelled from their districts and replaced by more affluent residents. Its drivers are structural — the policies and planning frameworks of the local state, and the tendency of capital to close rent gaps. It is, as the geographer Neil Smith put it, a “global urban strategy”.[\[10\]](https://www.common-wealth.org/interactive/the-greater-manchester-gentrification-index#fn) To live in a neighbourhood being gentrified is to experience rent rises, the destruction of community and ultimately displacement. Yet it is often something that is difficult to quantify and track."The Greater Manchester Gentrification Index (Common Wealth)

# Part 1 Univariate Visuals

## Labour Market Makeup and Gentrification

```{r}
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 8
library(readr)
library(janitor)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(modelsummary)
LongPanelPropj = read_csv("d:/PositStuff/gmpanel/LongPanelPropj.csv")
LongPanelProp = read_csv("d:/PositStuff/gmpanel/LongPanelProp.csv")
PanelLong = read_csv("d:/PositStuff/gmpanel/LongPanelProp.csv")
p1=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=graduate/(graduate+not_graduate),colour=location))+geom_line()+ylab("%Graduates")+theme_light()
p2=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=graduate/(graduate+not_graduate),colour=factor(gentrified)))+stat_summary(fun=mean,geom="line")+geom_jitter()+ylab("%Graduates")+theme_classic()+scale_color_discrete(name = "Group",labels = c("Neighbours","Historically gentrified"))+stat_summary(fun=mean,geom="point")
p9=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=routine_manual_occupations/(intermediate_occupations+routine_manual_occupations+never_worked_long_term_unemployed+higher_managerial_administrative_professional_occupations),colour=location))+geom_line()+ylab("%Manual")+theme_light()
p10=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=routine_manual_occupations/(intermediate_occupations+routine_manual_occupations+never_worked_long_term_unemployed+higher_managerial_administrative_professional_occupations),colour=factor(gentrified)))+stat_summary(fun=mean,geom="line")+geom_jitter()+ylab("%Manual")+theme_classic()+scale_color_discrete(name = "Group",labels = c("Neighbours","Historically gentrified"))+stat_summary(fun=mean,geom="point")
p11=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=higher_managerial_administrative_professional_occupations/(intermediate_occupations+routine_manual_occupations+never_worked_long_term_unemployed+higher_managerial_administrative_professional_occupations),colour=location))+geom_line()+ylab("%Higher_Managerial")+theme_light()
p12=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=higher_managerial_administrative_professional_occupations/(intermediate_occupations+routine_manual_occupations+never_worked_long_term_unemployed+higher_managerial_administrative_professional_occupations),colour=factor(gentrified)))+stat_summary(fun=mean,geom="line")+geom_jitter()+ylab("%Higher_Managerial")+theme_classic()+scale_color_discrete(name = "Group",labels = c("Neighbours","Historically gentrified"))+stat_summary(fun=mean,geom="point")
p13=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=never_worked_long_term_unemployed/(intermediate_occupations+routine_manual_occupations+never_worked_long_term_unemployed+higher_managerial_administrative_professional_occupations),colour=location))+geom_line()+ylab("%Unemployed")+theme_light()
p14=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=never_worked_long_term_unemployed/(intermediate_occupations+routine_manual_occupations+never_worked_long_term_unemployed+higher_managerial_administrative_professional_occupations),colour=factor(gentrified)))+stat_summary(fun=mean,geom="line")+geom_jitter()+ylab("%Unemployed")+theme_classic()+scale_color_discrete(name = "Group",labels = c("Neighbours","Historically gentrified"))+stat_summary(fun=mean,geom="point")
(p2/p1)|(p10/p9)|(p12/p11)|(p14/p13)
```

## Housing Market Makeup and Gentrification

~Comparatively larger increase in grads in gentrifying areas with divergence starting around 1991 census wave.following right to buy owner occupied tenure rises in gentrified areas between 1980-2000 but then drops and flatlines. Very low effect on non gentrified areas though.Following the peak in owner occupied tenure rented and other tenures in ancoats and quays massively overtake those in neighbors around 2000 proportional to the initial Right to Buy effect.~

Could be granger causal? Right to Buy -\> Lag-2Coucnil_tenure- -\> Lag-1Owner_tenure(+) -\>Renting Boom

```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 8
p3=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=local_authority_etc/(owner_occupied+other_rented+other_tenures+local_authority_etc),colour=location))+geom_line()+ylab("%LocalAuthority")+theme_light()
p4=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=local_authority_etc/(owner_occupied+other_rented+other_tenures+local_authority_etc),colour=factor(gentrified)))+stat_summary(fun=mean,geom="line")+geom_jitter()+ylab("%LocalAuthority")+theme_classic()+scale_color_discrete(name = "Group",labels = c("Neighbours","Historically gentrified"))+stat_summary(fun=mean,geom="point")
p5=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=owner_occupied/(owner_occupied+other_rented+other_tenures+local_authority_etc),colour=location))+geom_line()+ylab("%Owner_occupied")+theme_light()
p6=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=owner_occupied/(owner_occupied+other_rented+other_tenures+local_authority_etc),colour=factor(gentrified)))+stat_summary(fun=mean,geom="line")+geom_jitter()+ylab("%Owner_occupied")+theme_classic()+scale_color_discrete(name = "Group",labels = c("Neighbours","Historically gentrified"))+stat_summary(fun=mean,geom="point")
p7=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=(other_rented+other_tenures)/(owner_occupied+other_rented+other_tenures+local_authority_etc),colour=location))+geom_line()+
  ylab("%other_rented+tenures")+theme_light()
p8=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=(other_rented+other_tenures)/(owner_occupied+other_rented+other_tenures+local_authority_etc),colour=factor(gentrified)))+
stat_summary(fun=mean,geom="line")+geom_jitter()+ylab("%other_rented+tenures")+theme_classic()+scale_color_discrete(name = "Group",labels = c("Neighbours","Historically gentrified"))+stat_summary(fun=mean,geom="point")
(p4/p3)|(p6/p5)|(p8/p7)
```

## Country of Birth and Gentrification

~Housing Makeup and share of those born in UK don't seem to be that strongly associated with both groups experiencing similiar migration patterns with a notable exception of Europeans with notably parallel trends~

# Part 2 Multivariate Visuals with Ball Mapper.Does Gentrification Structurally Manifest in the Data?

^~Note that ancoats migrates from one ball to the next and eventually ends up in the high Grad% similiar housing market makeup alongside the quays by 2021. Note that on housing market makeup ancoats is most frequently similiar to chettam and quays to kersal. Note especially that in 1971 Quays had a housing market quite similiar to chettam and ancoats in 2011 and 2021 somewhat defying the trend~^

```{r}
#| fig-width: 18
#| fig-height: 10
#Simon Rudkin Didn't sponsor this I promise, i just found his posters very pretty and wanted to try and make some too#
library(BallMapper)
set.seed(123)
values = LongPanelPropj$GraduateP
points =  LongPanelPropj |> select(owner_occupiedP,local_authority_etcP,otherrented_tenuresP)
#One possible heuristic to set epsilon is to calculate common dispersion metrics for points specifically IQR/2(Probable error) and standard deviation
# In our case it turned out that the best representations are generated with e=0.17 or exactly one sd, for robustness its worthwhile to try other values between 0.17 and 0.14
ball = BallMapper::BallMapper(as.data.frame(points),as.data.frame(values),epsilon = 0.01)
ball = BallMapper::BallMapper(as.data.frame(points),as.data.frame(values),epsilon = 0.17) #epsilon 0.17 seems to preserve the complexity in the best way
ballassign = ball$points_covered_by_landmarks

#WARNING AI Generated Code as I am only learning how to properly add unit time labels to Ball Mapper Graphs#
library(igraph)
library(ggraph)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Number of nodes
n_nodes <- length(ball$coloring)

# 2. Calculate ball sizes from your ballassign indices
ball_sizes <- sapply(ball$points_covered_by_landmarks, length)

# 3. Generate unit-time labels for each ball
node_labels <- sapply(ball$points_covered_by_landmarks, function(indices) {
  subset_data <- PanelLong[indices, ]
  paste0(subset_data$location, "-", subset_data$year, collapse = "\n")
})

# 4. Build the vertices data frame safely
vertices_df <- data.frame(
  name = 1:n_nodes,
  label = node_labels,
  coloring = ball$coloring,
  size = ball_sizes
)

# 5. Create the igraph object
g <- graph_from_data_frame(d = ball$edges, vertices = vertices_df, directed = FALSE)
#Though I did customise the plot below though#
ggraph(g, layout = "stress") +
  geom_edge_link(alpha = 0.8, color = "gray60") +
  geom_node_point(aes(size = size, color = coloring)) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = label), repel = TRUE, size = 3.5, color = "black") +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option="D") +
  theme_light() +
  labs(title = "Ball Mapper Graph of gentrification - points in the same ball are closest on housing market makeup within +-17 percentage points",
       color = "%Graduates", size = "Ball Size(number of points)") + scale_size_continuous(range = c(6, 12))
```

# Part 3 What if? approximate counterfactuals with first differences

## Using First Differences allows one to remove time invariant unobservables and baselines and use changes in the neighbouring control wards as counterfactuals to what would have happened in Quays and Ancoats without the structural change. Robust to general UK trends such as immigration or Covid by exploiting within ward variation over time.Gap between group means can be interpreted as a simple DiD estimate for a particular period.

```{r}
LongPanelPropj <- LongPanelPropj |> 
  group_by(location) |> 
  mutate(across(
    .cols = c(
      GraduateP, local_authority_etcP, owner_occupiedP, otherrented_tenuresP, 
      BornUkP, BornEuropeP, BornRestP, WhiteP, BlackP, AsianP, OtherP, 
      unemployedP, intermediate_occupationsP, manualP, HighManegmentP
    ),
    .fns = ~ . - lag(.)
 
  ))
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 8
p17=ggplot(LongPanelPropj,aes(x=year,y=BornUkP,colour=factor(gentrified)))+stat_summary(fun=mean,geom="line")+ylab("10_year_Change_%BornUK")+theme_light()+scale_color_discrete(name = "Group",labels = c("Neighbours","Historically gentrified"))+stat_summary(fun=mean,geom="point")
```

## ~Across indicators it seems that the 1991-2001 gap has been a pivotal moment of divergence between the two groups corresponding to both the services boom and regeneration efforts by the GMP and local councils.This notably slightly misalligns with the ball mapper results which instead separate out ancoats and quays from the rest of the pack around 2011-2021. This however seems largely driven by a drop in owner occupied housing proportion between 2000-2010s and a renting boom happening around the same time. Therefore something interesting is at play - an increase in highly educated worker share preceded a renting boom and a relative drop in owner occupied housing. Regeneration may have slightly preceded gentrification indeed the decrease in unemployment relative to its neighbors also happens in the 2001 census period.~
